title: bug: fake-Docker browser receipt assertion still expects unredacted stderr
description:

comments.author: governor-12ae245c
comments.content:
GOVERNOR NOTE — a concern I raised against this row's framing, checked and WITHDRAWN. Recorded so the planner does not spend a step re-opening it.

In #workers (msg-c3a6d207) I warned that this might not be a stale assertion but an OVER-REDACTION defect in DONE task-c78140e9 — the theory being that `docker: not found` carries no secret, so blanketing it would mean that row traded a leak for a blindfold and every operator-facing refusal detail on this path went opaque. That theory is FALSE. I read the implementation; the filer's framing is correct and this row is aimed at the right side.

Why it is false, from `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ledger.ts` (note: `deployment/`, not `deploy/` as the description says — worth fixing so nobody greps the wrong path):
- `declassifyRefusal` keeps `code` and `layer` ALWAYS and declassifies only the free-text `detail`. `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE` is itself a member of `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS`, so the vocabulary every reader routes on is untouched. Nothing went opaque.
- The redacted value is raw tool stderr off `lastStderrLine`, which is the untrusted class by construction, not a benign message caught by a clumsy matcher.
- The allowlist is deliberate and its rationale is written at :30-38: a detector CANNOT recognise these secrets — an environment value is opaque and arrives inside a 600-byte stderr tail with no scheme, delimiter or header to match on. So the defence is a finite set of production-minted strings rather than pattern-matching. Membership is EXACT — no trim, no prefix, no case folding — precisely because `"<phase>: <tool output>"` is how a secret rides beside a safe word.

So DoD 1 is correctly aimed: update the consumer to the shipped redaction contract, keep the exact code/layer/dispatch-stage checks, and do not weaken production redaction. Concretely, do NOT "fix" this by adding `docker: not found` — or any stderr-derived string — to `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS`. That set may only ever contain strings minted by production code with no caller text in them; widening it to satisfy a test would reintroduce exactly the leak c78140e9 closed, and would do it in the one place designed to prevent it.

One process fact for whoever grades this: c78140e9 was gated on the daemon and control-room legs, and this red only appears in the browser lane, which was not in its gate set. The gate set did not reach the consumer; no reviewer skipped a step.
